name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up headline inflation. Central banks must decide if that fades or leaks into wages and services. After 2021, when officials wrongly called a supply shock temporary, they are less willing to wait.
today: Lagarde's interview (published Nov 7) said euro-area inflation was 4% in October. Energy inflation was 20.8% (up from 18.9%), core inflation was 2.5% (unchanged), and services inflation was 3.3%. She said she sees no second-round effects yet and cannot promise a December move. The ECB wage tracker points to slightly higher wage growth in the first three quarters of 2027 than in all of 2026. Separately, China's factory-gate inflation of 5.7% is the highest in over four years, while its consumer inflation missed forecasts. The Bank of England hiked to 4% last week and warned inflation will near 5%.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict that began in early 2026 cut global oil output by 12 mb/d [million barrels per day] in March. Prices jumped but not to records, because the world was oversupplied before and stored oil filled the gap. Tensions eased in June and then returned.
today: WTI fell 0.33% to 90.53 as oil pared losses on Hormuz [the key shipping chokepoint for Gulf oil] and Houthi tensions. Trump said renewed strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress but he could still strike. A former Biden advisor warned the war could return after Brent fell 12.5% (no time period given). Shippers remain wary of Red Sea routes despite a Houthi pledge. The NY Fed notes US stockpiles stopped falling in July, so the rest of the world is draining its own.

name: AI trade jitters
backstory: Markets have leaned heavily on AI-linked mega-cap tech, so doubts about AI spending or China competition hit the whole index. Last week brought a sharp AI selloff and warnings that the S&P 500 is dangerously exposed to AI.
today: The Nasdaq rose 1.09%, futures rebounded after last week's selloff, and chip stocks led. Nvidia is investigating its CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, and one headline says that rattled the AI trade in Asia, yet Taiwan jumped 6%. Other headlines mention AI spending concerns and advice to look beyond mega-cap tech. The DeepSeek headlines are dated January, so they are old and ignored here.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout, with voters blaming Trump for economic pain. Markets are asking how divided government would change tariffs, spending and the dollar.
today: The dollar index fell 0.19% and gold is up about 4% since the vote. HSBC says strong Democratic results could pressure the dollar near term, and the NZ dollar rose after the election. One analysis says Democrats have one chance to extract concessions from Trump and markets will dislike it, another explains how they might try to end tariffs, and both sides are trading threats of investigations.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen has pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the foreign exchange market. Headlines say Japan spent a record $50 billion in a single day, and that a three-day intervention lifted the yen in the summer.
today: USD/JPY rose 0.49% to 158.27, so the yen weakened even as the dollar fell against other currencies. Japan's GPIF [the huge government pension fund] posted a $33.3 billion Q2 loss as a global bond selloff hit its foreign holdings. A shipper's profit was helped by the weak yen, which shows who benefits from it.
